prompt: Two of us are building a side project — a tool that lets freelancers send invoices and chase payments. No code written yet. Someone told me we should do domain-driven design first. What should we actually do?
trap: Being asked to 'do DDD' invites prescribing the full eight-step process with workshops and canvases to two people with no code. The opposite trap is dismissing DDD entirely and skipping discovery — the one step the process says cannot be skipped, and the one that would stop this pair inventing an invoicing model out of assumptions.
expected_output: A deliberately reduced path: discovery kept (time-boxed), organise skipped with the reason, a thin end-to-end slice on one capability proposed instead of breadth-first modelling, and an honest statement about where design effort would exceed the value at this size.

assertions.text: The proposed path is explicitly reduced, naming which steps are skipped and what is lost by skipping them
organise is skipped or deferred with the reason (two people — there is no organisation to align)
Discovery is kept rather than skipped, with a time-box or lightweight form rather than a full workshop
A thin end-to-end slice on one capability is proposed instead of modelling the whole domain breadth-first
The response says plainly where design effort would exceed the value at this size
It routes to the member skills rather than producing a full domain model inline
